title: What build means, and what Vite does
summary: Separate source code, development serving, type checking, production bundling and local preview.

blocks.title: A build is inspection plus packaging, not publishing
blocks.body: Source files are written for people and tools. The build gate first asks TypeScript whether the code agrees with its types, then asks Vite to turn the app into optimized static files under dist. Deployment is the separate act of serving an accepted build at a URL.

blocks.heading: 3. The whole Vite config is small

blocks.title: Build is not proof of the whole experience
blocks.body: A passing build proves the source can type-check and bundle. It does not prove every page is readable, every interaction works, or the production domain serves the intended commit. Those need tests and visual verification.
